info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package analytics is product analytics: send an event, read back who did what.

get.summary: Returns one person's events across every tenant, newest first: what they did and the errors they hit, each with the org it was filed under, its session, page and product, and whether a platform operator wrote it acting as them.
get.description:
Returns one person's events across every tenant, newest first: what they
did and the errors they hit, each with the org it was filed under, its session,
page and product, and whether a platform operator wrote it acting as them.

The person is the IAM account <org>/<name>, matched by their IAM id, by
<org>/<name>, and by every anonymous visitor id an identify row linked to them —
so the visit before they signed in is in the history too. Default window 30d;
tenant narrows to one org; pages by keyset, so pass next back as cursor.
SuperAdmin only.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description: Org is the IAM org that owns the account, from the path.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the account's name within Org, from the path.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
ID is the account's IAM id (the token's sub) when the caller holds it already —
the directory row it opened. Given, IAM is not asked; empty, it is. It is matched
as given: a SuperAdmin naming another id reads that id's events, which they may
read anyway.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description:
Range is a relative window: a count and a unit — 24h, 7d, 90d, any <N>h or
<N>d — or day, week, month, all. Default 30d. Ignored when both start and end
are given.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Start is the inclusive lower bound of a custom window, RFC3339. Requires end.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: End is the exclusive upper bound of a custom window, RFC3339. Requires start.

parameters.name: tenant
parameters.description: Tenant keeps only the rows filed under this org. Empty reads every tenant.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit is how many rows to return, newest first. Default 100, at most 500.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Cursor continues a listing: pass back the previous page's next. Omit it for
the first page.

get.summary: Returns one person's visits across every tenant, the most recent first: when each began and ended, how many events and pages it held, the page it began on, whether a platform operator acted in it as them, and its session replay when one was recorded — the recording's length, activity, size and first page.
get.description:
Returns one person's visits across every tenant, the most recent first:
when each began and ended, how many events and pages it held, the page it began
on, whether a platform operator acted in it as them, and its session replay when
one was recorded — the recording's length, activity, size and first page. Open a
recorded visit at /sessions/{session} to replay it.

The person and the window are History's. SuperAdmin only.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description: Org is the IAM org that owns the account, from the path.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the account's name within Org, from the path.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
ID is the account's IAM id (the token's sub) when the caller holds it already —
the directory row it opened. Given, IAM is not asked; empty, it is. It is matched
as given: a SuperAdmin naming another id reads that id's events, which they may
read anyway.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description:
Range is a relative window: a count and a unit — 24h, 7d, 90d, any <N>h or
<N>d — or day, week, month, all. Default 30d. Ignored when both start and end
are given.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Start is the inclusive lower bound of a custom window, RFC3339. Requires end.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: End is the exclusive upper bound of a custom window, RFC3339. Requires start.

parameters.name: tenant
parameters.description:
Tenant counts only the events filed under this org, so a visit that crossed
tenants is summarized from its rows here alone. Empty reads every tenant.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Limit is how many visits to return, the most recent first. Default 100, at
most 500.

get.summary: Session returns one visit of one person, ready to replay: the visit, every event the person sent in it oldest first, and the recording — each stored block and whether it could be read, and the rrweb frames in order, verbatim, for an rrweb player.
get.description:
Session returns one visit of one person, ready to replay: the visit, every event
the person sent in it oldest first, and the recording — each stored block and
whether it could be read, and the rrweb frames in order, verbatim, for an rrweb
player. A visit that was not recorded answers with its events and no frames.

The visit must be the person's: a session id the plane holds none of their events
under is 404, whoever else it belongs to. A recording is read only from the
replay pipeline's own bucket, and an answer carries at most 32 MiB of frames —
past that, truncated is true. SuperAdmin only.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description: Org is the IAM org that owns the account, from the path.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name is the account's name within Org, from the path.

parameters.name: session
parameters.description: Session is the visit's session id, from the path.

post.summary: Capture product events into your org's warehouse
post.description:
Stores pageviews, browser errors, identifies and custom commerce events as rows in the caller's own tenant, and answers a receipt {accepted, dropped} that always totals what was sent — a beacon is never silently discarded.

THE STATUS SAYS WHETHER ANYTHING LANDED, so a green check can never mean an empty warehouse. 200 means at least one event was stored (or that nothing was sent), and a nonzero `dropped` beside a nonzero `accepted` is a PARTIAL batch, never a failed one — a batch is not refused whole for its worst element. If NOTHING was stored the request is an error, and it names the one thing that fixes it: 401 `ingest_key_required` when every event was refused for want of a credential (the same events land with a key), and 400 `unroutable_events` when the caller HAD capability and the body still named nothing storable.

ONE endpoint for every wire a Hanzo surface emits, dispatched by the SHAPE of the body and never by a second path: a bare event object, a bare array of them, the {batch:[…]} / {events:[…]} envelope, the team console's snake_case array, and the PostHog wire (spelled `distinct_id`/`api_key`, which the canonical wire never uses). BATCH IS A BODY, NOT A PATH — there is no /v1/event/batch, because an array already is one.

WHAT THE CALLER PRESENTS DECIDES WHAT IT MAY WRITE, and the endpoint itself grants nothing. A validated bearer or an org API key writes the full event at full fidelity. A PUBLISHABLE key (pk-, on Authorization: Bearer, x-hanzo-ingest-key, or ?ingest_key= for navigator.sendBeacon, which cannot set headers) does the same, and is the credential a browser bundle ships: it is deliberately NOT a secret, it resolves WHICH tenant a beacon belongs to and nothing more. A pk- never authenticates and can READ NOTHING — not this org's errors, not a lens, not any other route on this API — so a leaked one lets a stranger write into your stream, and never lets one read out of it. Reading these rows back always takes a real bearer. A Hanzo Team space token resolves its org at REDUCED capability: the signed account names the person, so a `distinctId` in the body cannot pin events on a colleague.

NO CREDENTIAL IS REFUSED: a write the server cannot attribute to a project is 401 `ingest_key_required`, and a credential that IS presented but resolves to no project is 403 `ingest_key_unknown`. Nothing is filed under a shared tenant — events nobody can read are worse than events nobody sent, because the caller is told it succeeded. A browser bundle therefore always ships a pk-, which is what /v1/event/tag.js takes.

THE STREAM IS FIRST PARTY. Every visitor's events are kept — page views, events, errors, identifies and the anonymous id — whatever they chose and under Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track alike: it is the org's own analytics, never sold or shared. Consent governs the third parties alone. Each event states the categories its visitor allowed in its `consent` property (`analytics,marketing,ads`), and that is all it may be forwarded under: Google Analytics needs analytics, the Meta pixel marketing, ad personalization ads. GPC or DNT on the request forwards nothing in any region (`consent_mode`: eu, us_privacy or global, from the country and US state the edge attests), whatever the event stated, and is stamped `refused`.

A REDUCED principal — a Hanzo Team space token — writes through the PROJECTION into its own org: narrowed to what the SERVER can name (pageviews and errors, plus the closed autocapture vocabulary $click, $input, $change, $submit, $view), where every one of those names is resolved through a server-owned table and stored as that table's value, so the name on the wire is never the name in the row. Stripped, too, to the fields the projection names, so revenue, personId, groupId and every property but the element annotation cannot reach a row — and an exception is carried only on an error, never on an interaction, so a click cannot ship a stack trace into a row's attributes. It does NOT name the person: the signed account is the identity, so a `distinctId` in the body cannot pin events on a colleague. Everything refused is counted in `dropped`.

The projected lane alone is bounded: 413 over 64 KiB, 400 over 50 events, 429 on the per-client-IP and per-peer caps. Two stored values carry their own bounds on top, because a request cap does not bound one value: an element annotation over 2 KiB (or a trail over 32 steps) and an exception class over 256 bytes are dropped from the row, which still lands. Authenticated bodies are offered to the observability plane first, which claims LLM-observability ingestion batches and declines everything else.

get.summary: Returns, oldest first and paged, the payments the caller's org made or received in a year, with the ones a correction restates named and what either party disputes — for the org's admins.
get.description:
Returns, oldest first and paged, the payments the caller's org made or received in
a year, with the ones a correction restates named and what either party disputes
— for the org's admins.

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: Year is the calendar year to read, UTC.

parameters.name: counterparty
parameters.description: Counterparty keeps only payments with this org on the other side.

parameters.name: rail
parameters.description: Rail keeps only payments that moved on this rail.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Cursor continues from the next of the page before; empty starts the year.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit is how many events to answer, default 100 and at most 1000.

post.summary: Records that the caller's org disputes one payment it is party to — for the org's admins.
post.description:
Records that the caller's org disputes one payment it is party to — for the org's
admins. A dispute is a record both parties read beside the payment, and it changes
nothing about it: the amount, the parties and the tax year stay as the rail stated
them, because only the rail that moved the money restates a payment.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's most recently captured errors, newest first.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's most recently captured errors, newest first. The
error-tracking read view over event.error — the plane table the write core's error
facts land in (errors are DELIBERATELY not on event.event) — each with its captured
exception surfaced from the attributes map as a first-class field.

The org is the validated principal's — never a parameter — and this read requires a
real bearer, NEVER the write-only publishable key: pk- can attribute a write and can
read nothing. 401 without a validated bearer, 503 when the warehouse is unreachable.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Limit is how many rows to return, newest first. Default 50, maximum 200; a
value at or below zero, or one that is not a number, takes the default.

get.summary: Reports whether the event plane can take a write and the warehouse can answer a read.
get.description:
Reports whether the event plane can take a write and the warehouse can
answer a read.

It reports the analytics subsystem's own liveness in BOTH directions: plane is
the event plane it WRITES (the bus and the JetStream stream every accepted
event is published to, both named in the report), and datastore is the
warehouse it READS, with each read lens's table reported as it is provisioned
(the LLM usage ledger and the product-event table).

EITHER ONE DOWN IS A 503, and the report says WHICH — they are probed
independently and never collapse into a single bit. A readiness gate on this
endpoint therefore gates on the write path as well as the read path: it
answers ready only when POST /v1/event can publish.

plane.ready IS A REAL PROBE and walks the ingest path itself — the same
connection and the same stream a publish uses — so it cannot answer ready while
a publish would 503. plane.reason carries the plane's own error text when it is
false.

datastore IS NOT PROBED WITH A QUERY. It is the state of the process's own
shared client — established, and not since closed — so a warehouse accepting
connections and failing reads still reports true. Degraded CARRIES the report
(status, the failing half, reason) as its body rather than an error envelope,
so a gate reads the cause off the same object it got at 200.

A MISSING LENS TABLE IS NOT A FAILURE and never moves the status: a lens
reported available:false answers honest-empty rather than erroring, so a fresh
deployment whose collector has not emitted yet is legitimately 200 with the
product-event lens unavailable. The lens block is reported whenever the
warehouse is REACHABLE — including on a report degraded by the plane, where the
tables genuinely were probed — and is absent only when the warehouse is not,
having nothing to say about tables it could not reach.

Unauthenticated on purpose — liveness has to be probe-able — and it reads NO
tenant data: table existence and stream presence only, never a row and never an
event.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's most recent product events, newest first.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's most recent product events, newest first.
The console's raw-event view over event.event — the same table the capture endpoints
fill — one row per stored event, with the row's attributes returned as the
properties object.

What a platform operator did acting as someone else is left out unless impersonated
asks for it; such a row carries impersonated and impersonated_by in its properties.

The org is the validated principal's — never a parameter — and a read requires a
real bearer, never the write-only publishable key. 401 without a validated bearer,
400 on an unknown impersonated value, 503 when the warehouse is unreachable.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Limit is how many rows to return, newest first. Default 50, maximum 200; a
value at or below zero, or one that is not a number, takes the default.

parameters.name: impersonated
parameters.description:
Impersonated is which events to return against the mark a platform operator
leaves acting as someone else: exclude (the default, the tenant's own
traffic), include, or only. Anything else is a 400.

get.summary: Reports that the unified insights surface is serving.
get.description:
Reports that the unified insights surface is serving. It reads no
tenant data and consults no dependency, so it answers 200 unconditionally and needs
no principal — liveness must be probe-able. The warehouse-connectivity probe is a
different question and lives at GET /v1/event/health.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's analytics KPIs for one time window.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's analytics KPIs for one time window. Three lenses
over one warehouse: llm is the live per-org LLM usage ledger (requests, tokens,
spend, models, providers, errors) and is always real; web (pageviews, visitors,
sessions) and commerce (orders, revenue, AOV) read the product-event table and
report available=false rather than fabricating zeros when it holds nothing yet.

The web and commerce lenses count the tenant's own traffic: what a platform
operator did while acting as someone else is left out unless impersonated asks for
it (include, or only). The LLM lens reads the usage ledger, which carries no such
mark, and counts every call.

The org is the validated principal's — never a parameter — so a caller can only
ever read its own tenant. 401 without a validated bearer, 400 on an unknown range
or impersonated value, 503 when the warehouse is unreachable.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description:
Range is a relative window: a count and a unit — 24h, 7d, 90d, any <N>h or
<N>d — or day, week, month, all. Default 24h. Ignored when both start and
end are given. An unknown value, or one past the 730-day horizon, is a 400.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Start is the inclusive lower bound of a custom window, RFC3339. Requires end.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: End is the exclusive upper bound of a custom window, RFC3339. Requires start.

parameters.name: impersonated
parameters.description:
Impersonated is which events the product-event lenses count against the mark
a platform operator leaves acting as someone else: exclude (the default, the
tenant's own traffic), include, or only. Anything else is a 400.

get.summary: A site's default pixel — a page view from an image, for a page that runs no script
get.description: Answers a transparent 1x1 GIF and records one page view for the project whose publishable key names the address: The page is `?u=` when given, else the Referer. The visitor is stamped from the request like every event, is one visitor for a day, and carries no cookie. Every view is recorded: it is the site's own first-party analytics. `?consent=analytics`, the visitor's choice as the embedding page knows it, is what it may be forwarded to Google Analytics under; Do-not-track and Global Privacy Control forward nothing, and a developer's own machine records nothing. The image is answered whatever happened to the view, with no-store.

post.description:
Accepts a batch of rrweb events from a browser recorder and hands it to the session-replay pipeline, which stores the recording and derives the session summary a player reads back.

ONE REQUEST IS ONE BATCH, and it is all-or-nothing: the recording is made durable before this answers, so a 200 {"accepted":1} means stored and never "buffered somewhere". There is no partial count, because a half-written recording is not a recording.

`sessionId` is REQUIRED and bounded — at most 70 characters of ASCII letters, digits or '-'. It is the key every batch of one visit is grouped and ordered by, so an id outside that grammar is refused 400 here rather than accepted and dropped further down. `windowId` separates two tabs of one session and `distinctId` attributes the recording to a person; both are optional. `events` is the rrweb batch, each element a raw eventWithTime object, carried VERBATIM — the summary (click, keypress and mouse-activity counts, size) is derived downstream from exactly these bytes, so nothing is re-encoded or dropped.

THE CALLER'S CREDENTIAL DECIDES THE TENANT, and the body never does: the recording lands in the org the presented credential resolves to. It takes the SAME credentials as /v1/event — a validated bearer, an org API key, or a publishable pk- key on Authorization: Bearer, x-hanzo-ingest-key or ?ingest_key= — so a browser bundle already holding a pk- for events needs nothing new to record. A caller that presents nothing is 401 `ingest_key_required`; one whose key resolves to no project is 403 `ingest_key_unknown`; a reduced principal (a Hanzo Team space token) is 403 `insufficient_capability`, because a full-fidelity screen recording has no projected form that is safe for a guest to write into a host org.

BOUNDS: 413 over 512 KiB of body, and that is the only bound on one batch — a recorder is expected to chunk a long session rather than send it whole, and the cap is the size one message can carry rather than an arbitrary number. 503 when the pipeline cannot take the batch: honest unavailability the caller can retry, never a 200 over a discarded recording.

put.summary: Upload a sourcemap for a release
put.description:
Stores the sourcemap of one generated script under a release, so browser errors from that release are reported, and grouped, by their original file, line and function. Frames are mapped when an error event is ingested, before it is grouped, so a fault keeps one issue across deploys that rebuild its bundle.

The body is the .map file (Source Map v3; index maps with `sections` are refused 422). `release` is the value the bundle sends as its events' `release` — the build's git sha — and `file` is the path the generated script is served at. Uploading the same release and file again replaces the map.

MAPS ARE PRIVATE. They are kept in the org's storage and never served; there is no route that reads one back. A build should remove the .map files from what it publishes once they are uploaded.

WHO MAY CALL: the org's own build identity — an IAM application token acting as itself, such as the CI application a hanzoai/ci run exchanges its ID token for. The map is filed under the org the token belongs to; naming another org is 403. A person's token, an org API key, and a token acting for someone else are 403; no credential is 401.

BOUNDS: 413 over 15 MiB of body. 503 when storage is unavailable.

parameters.name: release
parameters.description: The release the bundle was stamped with: the git sha of the build, the same value its error events send as `release`.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The path the generated script is served at, such as /assets/index-3f9a.js. A full URL is accepted; scheme, host, query and fragment are dropped.

get.summary: The Hanzo event tag — the one-line install for a surface with no bundler
get.description:
Serves the browser tag that autocaptures pageviews (initial and SPA) and uncaught errors onto the canonical wire at POST /v1/event.

Install is one line, and it is the same line for a Hanzo property and for a customer's own page:

    <script defer src="https://api.hanzo.ai/v1/event/tag.js" data-key="pk-…"></script>

`data-key` is the publishable key the project mints; `data-product` optionally names the emitting surface. The key may also ride the src as `?key=` for a host that strips data attributes.

THE STREAM IS FIRST PARTY; THE THIRD PARTIES FOLLOW THE VISITOR'S REGION. Every page view, event, error and identify goes to the site's own stream for every visitor, under its anonymous id and session, whatever they chose and under Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track alike: it is the site's own analytics, never sold or shared. The rule for Google Analytics, the Meta pixel and the other platforms is the one GET /v1/project/tags serves for the visitor's region. `eu` (the EU, the EEA, the UK, Switzerland, and any visitor no edge placed): Google Analytics runs for everyone under Consent Mode v2 with all four flags denied (cookieless) and is upgraded by Performance and Targeted Advertising; Meta is init'ed after `fbq('consent','revoke')` and sends nothing until Marketing; no other platform loads before a choice. `us_privacy` (a US state with a privacy law, or no attested state) and `global`: everything runs at once under Consent Mode granted, and Targeted Advertising off is exactly `fbq('dataProcessingOptions',['LDU'],0,0)` and ad_storage, ad_user_data and ad_personalization denied. Under GPC or DNT no third party loads in any region, Google Analytics included. The choice is the `__Host-hz_consent` cookie, written by the @hanzo/ui consent banner or this tag's own, beside the version and the rule it was made under: `eu` counts only a choice made under `eu`, and the policy floor voids a choice's grants, never its refusals. Each event states the grants in force when it is sent, and that is what cloud may forward under.

`data-banner` draws Hanzo's consent design by region. In `eu`, for a visitor who has not chosen and whose browser has not refused: a card with Manage preferences, Accept all and a × that keeps essential cookies only, so refusing is as easy as accepting. In `global`, a notice ("We use cookies to improve your experience. By continuing to browse, you agree.") until the visitor closes it with ×. In `us_privacy`, no card: a "Your Privacy Choices" link with the opt-out icon at the foot of the page, unless the page carries its own (an element marked `data-hz-consent-link`). Manage preferences or the link opens the sheet — Strictly Necessary Cookies (always active, the site's own first-party analytics included), Performance (Google Analytics), Marketing (the Meta pixel), and Sell, Share, or Use Your Data for Targeted Advertising, each chosen apart; outside `eu` each is on by default and Targeted Advertising off is the opt-out. Withdrawing a category clears the third-party cookies it allowed, on every domain above the page, and never an essential one. The sheet links only the policies the page names: `data-cookies` its cookie policy, `data-banner`'s value its privacy policy, `data-terms` its terms. `window.hzConsent.open()` opens the sheet again from a page's own link.

WITHOUT A KEY THE TAG SENDS NOTHING. A keyless beacon is accepted 200 into $public, a reserved tenant the owning org cannot read — so silence is the honest failure, and the tag picks it rather than reporting success into a tenant nobody reads.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's LLM usage over time as an evenly-spaced series.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's LLM usage over time as an evenly-spaced series.
One point per hour or per day — the bucket the window implies, 24h giving hours and
7d/30d giving days — carrying requests, total tokens and spend in cents. Empty
buckets are filled with zeros so a client charts a continuous line.

The org is the validated principal's — never a parameter. 401 without a validated
bearer, 400 on an unknown range, 503 when the warehouse is unreachable.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description:
Range is a relative window: a count and a unit — 24h, 7d, 90d, any <N>h or
<N>d — or day, week, month, all. Default 24h. Ignored when both start and
end are given. An unknown value, or one past the 730-day horizon, is a 400.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Start is the inclusive lower bound of a custom window, RFC3339. Requires end.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: End is the exclusive upper bound of a custom window, RFC3339. Requires start.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's ranked lenses for one window, five of them at once.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's ranked lenses for one window, five of them at once.
models ranks LLM models by spend and is always real; products ranks commerce orders
by revenue; topPages ranks requested paths, topReferrers the external referrer
domains ("(direct)" for a missing or same-origin one) and topSources the utm_source
campaigns ("(none)" when absent), each by pageviews. Every lens carries each row's
share of the in-window total, so a top-N honestly shows the long tail.

The four event lenses report available=false rather than fabricating zeros when the
product-event table holds nothing yet, and count the tenant's own traffic: what a
platform operator did acting as someone else is left out unless impersonated asks
for it (include, or only). Models reads the usage ledger, which carries no such
mark. The org is the validated principal's — never a parameter. 401 without a
validated bearer, 400 on an unknown range or impersonated value, 503 when the
warehouse is unreachable.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description:
Range is a relative window: a count and a unit — 24h, 7d, 90d, any <N>h or
<N>d — or day, week, month, all. Default 24h. Ignored when both start and
end are given. An unknown value, or one past the 730-day horizon, is a 400.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Start is the inclusive lower bound of a custom window, RFC3339. Requires end.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: End is the exclusive upper bound of a custom window, RFC3339. Requires start.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Limit bounds every ranked lens in the response. Default 10, maximum 100; a
value at or below zero, or one that is not a number, takes the default.

parameters.name: impersonated
parameters.description:
Impersonated is which events the product-event lenses count against the mark
a platform operator leaves acting as someone else: exclude (the default, the
tenant's own traffic), include, or only. Anything else is a 400.

available.description: Available is false when the product-event table could not be read.

items.description: Items is the ranked buckets, most pageviews first. Empty rather than absent.

reason.description: Reason says why the lens is unavailable. Omitted when it is available.

source.description: Source is the warehouse table the lens read.

key.description:
Key is the bucket: a requested path, a referrer domain ("(direct)" for none or
a same-origin one), or a utm_source ("(none)" when absent).

pageviews.description: Pageviews is how many $pageview events fell in this bucket.

pct.description:
Pct is this bucket's share of ALL in-window pageviews, 0..100, one decimal —
not of the returned rows, so a top-N shows the long tail honestly.

visitors.description: Visitors is how many distinct people they came from.

aov.description:
AOV is average order value — Revenue/Orders, rounded to two places. Zero when
there were no orders.

available.description:
Available is false when the product-event table could not be read — the lens is
reported missing rather than as zeros that look like no sales.

orders.description: Orders is how many order_completed events landed in the window.

reason.description: Reason says why the lens is unavailable. Omitted when it is available.

revenue.description: Revenue is the total those orders carried, in the events' own currency unit.

source.description: Source is the warehouse table the lens read.

at.description: At is when the dispute was filed, unix seconds.

by.description: By is the org that disputes it: one of the event's two parties.

event.description: Event is the id of the event disputed.

reason.description: Reason is what the party says is wrong.

agent.description:
Agent is the principal that acted for the buyer, as IAM names it. Only the
buyer's copy carries it: it may name a person, and who inside the buyer
acted is none of the seller's records.

at.description: At is when the payment was made, unix seconds, as the rail recorded it.

buyer.description: Buyer is the org that paid.

category.description:
Category is what the payment was for — service, goods, transfer, refund or
royalty — as the rail recorded the parties agreeing it. Empty on an event
stated before version 2, and on a rail that records no purpose.

chain.description: Chain is the CAIP-2 network an on-chain payment moved on.

corrects.description: Corrects is the id of the event this one restates, when it is a correction.

currency.description: Currency is what the amounts are in: an ISO 4217 code or an asset symbol.

fee.description: Fee is what the rail kept of Gross, an exact decimal in Currency.

fmv.description:
FMV is Gross's fair market value in U.S. dollars when it was paid, an exact
decimal.

gross.description: Gross is what the buyer paid, an exact decimal in Currency.

id.description: ID is the event's identity, derived from its rail and proof.

jurisdictions.description:
Jurisdictions are the ISO 3166 codes the payment is subject to, when the
rail knows them.

parent.description:
Parent is the agent that spawned Agent, when one did. Only the buyer's copy
carries it, for Agent's reason.

proof.description:
Proof is the rail's own reference for the payment: a settlement id, a chain
transaction hash or a processor reference.

rail.description:
Rail is how the money moved: x402, ledger, chain, ach, wire, card, network
or other.

seller.description: Seller is the org that was paid.

service.description: Service is what was bought, in the rail's own words.

tax.description: Tax is the tax collected within Gross, an exact decimal in Currency.

tx.description: Tx is the on-chain transaction hash of an on-chain payment.

v.description: V is the schema version the event was stated in.

disputes.description:
Disputes are what either party has disputed about the events in Rows. A
dispute changes nothing about the event it names.

next.description: Next continues the read; empty on the last page.

superseded.description: Superseded are the ids in Rows that a correction restates.

available.description:
Available is true whenever the ledger answered — including with no usage in the
window, which is honest zeros rather than a missing lens.

completionTokens.description: CompletionTokens is the output half of Tokens.

errorRate.description:
ErrorRate is Errors/Requests, 0..1, rounded to three places. Zero when there
were no requests.

errors.description: Errors is how many of Requests failed.

models.description: Models is how many distinct models the org called.

promptTokens.description: PromptTokens is the input half of Tokens.

providers.description: Providers is how many distinct providers served them.

requests.description: Requests is how many LLM calls the org made in the window.

source.description: Source is the warehouse table the lens read.

spendCents.description: SpendCents is what those calls cost, in cents.

tokens.description: Tokens is prompt plus completion tokens over those calls.

model.description: Model is the model id, e.g. zen5-coder.

pct.description: Pct is this model's share of the window's returned spend, 0..100, one decimal.

requests.description: Requests is how many calls went to this model.

spendCents.description: SpendCents is what they cost, in cents.

tokens.description: Tokens is prompt plus completion tokens over those calls.

commerce.description: Commerce is the orders/revenue lens over product events.

end.description: End is the window's exclusive upper bound, RFC3339 UTC.

impersonated.description:
Impersonated is which events web and commerce counted against the mark a
platform operator leaves acting as someone else: exclude (the tenant's own
traffic), include, or only. LLM reads the usage ledger, which carries no mark.

interval.description: Interval is the bucket width the window implies: hour or day.

llm.description: LLM is the LLM usage lens — real per-org data.

range.description: Range is the window that was actually applied: 24h, 7d, 30d or custom.

scope.description: Scope names the tenant these numbers belong to.

start.description: Start is the window's inclusive lower bound, RFC3339 UTC.

web.description: Web is the web-traffic lens over product events.

orders.description: Orders is how many order_completed events carried it.

productId.description: ProductID is the product the order events named.

revenue.description: Revenue is the total they carried, in the events' own currency unit.

units.description: Units is the summed quantity sold.

org.description:
Org is the IAM org slug the rows were read under: the validated principal's,
resolved server-side.

end.description: End is the window's exclusive upper bound, RFC3339 UTC.

interval.description: Interval is the bucket width: hour or day.

range.description: Range is the window that was actually applied: 24h, 7d, 30d or custom.

scope.description: Scope names the tenant these numbers belong to.

series.description: Series is one point per bucket, oldest first, with empty buckets zero-filled.

source.description: Source is the warehouse table the series read.

start.description: Start is the window's inclusive lower bound, RFC3339 UTC.

end.description: End is the window's exclusive upper bound, RFC3339 UTC.

impersonated.description:
Impersonated is which events products, topPages, topReferrers and topSources
counted against the mark a platform operator leaves acting as someone else:
exclude (the tenant's own traffic), include, or only. Models reads the usage
ledger, which carries no mark.

models.description: Models ranks the window's LLM models by spend — real per-org data.

products.description: Products ranks the window's products by revenue.

range.description: Range is the window that was actually applied: 24h, 7d, 30d or custom.

scope.description: Scope names the tenant these rankings belong to.

start.description: Start is the window's inclusive lower bound, RFC3339 UTC.

topPages.description: Pages ranks the paths visitors requested, by pageviews.

topReferrers.description: Referrers ranks the external domains visitors arrived from, by pageviews.

topSources.description: Sources ranks the utm_source campaigns visitors arrived on, by pageviews.

available.description: Available is true whenever the ledger answered, including with no rows.

items.description: Items is the ranked models, highest spend first.

source.description: Source is the warehouse table the lens read.

available.description: Available is false when the product-event table could not be read.

items.description: Items is the ranked products, highest revenue first. Empty rather than absent.

reason.description: Reason says why the lens is unavailable. Omitted when it is available.

source.description: Source is the warehouse table the lens read.

requests.description: Requests is how many LLM calls fell in this bucket.

spendCents.description: SpendCents is what they cost, in cents.

t.description: T is the bucket's start, RFC3339 UTC, aligned to the interval.

tokens.description: Tokens is prompt plus completion tokens over those calls.

available.description:
Available is false when the product-event table could not be read — the lens is
reported missing rather than as zeros that look like real traffic.

pageviews.description: Pageviews is how many $pageview events landed in the window.

reason.description: Reason says why the lens is unavailable. Omitted when it is available.

sessions.description: Sessions is how many distinct visits they span.

source.description: Source is the warehouse table the lens read.

visitors.description: Visitors is how many distinct people those pageviews came from.

distinctId.description:
DistinctID is the person/visitor the error is attributed to. Omitted when the
row carries none.

event.description: Event is the event name the error was stored under, e.g. $error.

exception.description:
Exception is the captured error itself — the {type, message, stack, handled}
object, already redacted at the fold point. Omitted when the row has none.

id.description:
ID is the row's stable event id — the client's own idempotency id when it sent
one, else the server-minted one.

library.description: Library is the client SDK that reported the error. Omitted when absent.

libraryVersion.description: LibraryVer is that SDK's version. Omitted when absent.

path.description: Path is the URL's path component. Omitted when absent.

product.description: Product is the surface that emitted the error. Omitted when absent.

properties.description:
Properties is the row's whole property bag, returned verbatim as stored — any
JSON object, $exception included. Omitted when the row carries none or it did
not parse.

sessionId.description: SessionID groups the events of one visit. Omitted when the client sent none.

timestamp.description: Timestamp is when the error was captured, RFC3339 UTC.

url.description: URL is the full page address the error fired on. Omitted when absent.

event.description: Event is the id of the economic event disputed.

reason.description: Reason is what the caller's org says is wrong, at most 1024 characters.

data.description: Data is the errors, newest first. Empty rather than absent when there are none.
Data is the events, newest first. Empty rather than absent when there are none.

available.description: Available reports whether that table exists in the warehouse right now.

table.description: Table is the fully-qualified warehouse table the lens reads.

events.description:
Events is the web/commerce lens (event.fact, signal='act'), honest-empty until the
collector emits.

llm.description: LLM is the live per-org usage ledger lens (hanzo.cloud_usage).

bus.description: Bus is the address this process reaches the plane at.

ready.description: Ready reports whether an ingest would succeed right now. False is a 503.

reason.description: Reason is the plane's own failure text, present only when Ready is false.

stream.description: Stream is the JetStream stream every signal lands on.

datastore.description:
Datastore reports whether the shared warehouse client has a live connection.
It is load-bearing for the READ path: false is one of the two ways this
answers 503.

lenses.description:
Lenses is per-lens table availability, probed only when connected — so it is
absent from a degraded report, which has nothing to say about tables it could
not reach.

lost.description:
Lost is the count of facts the sink irrecoverably dropped since boot
(warehouse.go). It is reported on the DEGRADED report too, and deliberately: a
warehouse that is unreachable is exactly when facts start failing their
deliveries, so suppressing the number here would hide it precisely when it
moves. ANY NON-ZERO VALUE IS AN ALARM — it counts data the endpoint already
answered 200 for.

plane.description:
Plane reports the event plane — the bus and the stream every accepted event is
published to BEFORE any of it reaches the warehouse. It is load-bearing for the
WRITE path: warehouse connectivity alone says nothing about whether a publish
can land, so the probe reports the write path from the write path itself.

reason.description: Reason is the human-readable cause, present only on a degraded report.

service.description:
Service names the subsystem answering, so a probe aggregating several health
endpoints can attribute a degraded one.

status.description:
Status is ok or degraded. Degraded is the 503 and means EITHER load-bearing
dependency is down — the warehouse this subsystem reads, or the event plane it
writes. It is not moved by a missing lens table, which is honest-empty.

warehouse.description: Warehouse names the datastore database every lens reads.

data.description: Data is the person and the page. Null when the read failed.

degraded.description:
Degraded names a source that did not answer — "iam" — so a person matched by
<owner>/<name> alone reads as an outage rather than as a quiet history.

msg.description: Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error", empty otherwise.

next.description: Next is the cursor for the following page, empty on the last one.

status.description: Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way.

engine.description: Engine names the engine serving the surface: hanzo-analytics.

ok.description: OK is always true — reaching this route is the liveness fact it reports.

surface.description: Surface is the path prefix this status covers: /v1/event/insights.

exhausted.description: Exhausted counts facts the bus abandoned after maxDeliver failed inserts.

undecodable.description: Undecodable counts messages acked without landing because they did not parse.

attested.description:
Attested is true when the identity boundary verified the writer as this
person — their IAM id or <owner>/<name>. False means a client named them,
which any holder of a publishable key can: a visitor before sign-in, or a
claim nobody vouched for.

distinctId.description: DistinctID is the id the event was attributed to — one of the person's ids.

event.description: Event is the event name, e.g. page_viewed or signup_completed.

id.description: ID is the row's stable event id.

impersonated.description:
Impersonated is true when a platform operator wrote the event acting as
someone else.

impersonatedBy.description: ImpersonatedBy is that operator, as <owner>/<name>. Omitted otherwise.

message.description: Message is an error's message, already redacted at ingest. Omitted on an act.

org.description:
Org is the tenant the event was filed under — the org that admitted it,
which need not be the account's own.

path.description: Path is the URL's path component. Omitted when absent.

product.description: Product is the surface that emitted the event. Omitted when absent.

sessionId.description: SessionID is the visit the event belongs to. Omitted when the client sent none.

signal.description: Signal is act for something the person did and error for a failure they hit.

timestamp.description: Timestamp is when it happened, RFC3339 UTC with the plane's nanoseconds.

type.description: Type is the kind within the signal: page, track, identify or group for an act.

url.description: URL is the page the event fired on. Omitted when absent.

events.description: Events is the page, newest first. Empty rather than absent when there are none.

person.description: Person is who the events are about, and every id they were matched by.

email.description:
Email is the account's address as IAM holds it. Empty when IAM did not answer
or holds none.

id.description:
ID is the account's IAM id, the token's sub. Empty when IAM did not answer,
which degraded then names.

ids.description:
IDs is every id this person's events were matched by: the IAM id,
<owner>/<name>, and each anonymous visitor id an identify row linked to them,
the links a verified write made first.

keys.description:
Keys is the two ids that are the account itself: the IAM id and
<owner>/<name>. A row is attested when the boundary verified one of these.

name.description: Name is the account's name within Owner.

owner.description: Owner is the IAM org that owns the account.

partial.description:
Partial is true when more visitor ids were linked than one read matches by,
so the oldest unverified links were left out.

end.description: End is the visit's last event, RFC3339 UTC.

events.description: Events is how many events the person sent in the visit.

impersonated.description:
Impersonated is true when a platform operator wrote any event of the visit
acting as someone else.

orgs.description:
Orgs is every tenant the visit's events were filed under: a visit that
crossed from a site into the console spans both.

pages.description: Pages is how many of them were page views.

product.description: Product is the surface the visit was on.

recording.description: Recording is the visit's session replay, or null when nothing was recorded.

start.description: Start is the visit's first event, RFC3339 UTC.

url.description: URL is the first page of the visit.

blocks.description:
Blocks is each stored block of the recording and whether it was read. Empty
when nothing was recorded.

events.description:
Events is every event the person sent in the visit, oldest first, so a player
can lay them on the recording's timeline.

frames.description:
Frames is the recording, oldest first: the rrweb events to replay. Empty when
nothing was recorded or nothing could be read.

person.description: Person is who the visit is about.

truncated.description:
Truncated is true when the recording was longer than one answer carries and
Frames stops early.

data.description: Data is the visit. Null when the read failed.

degraded.description: Degraded names a source that did not answer: "iam", or "replay".

msg.description: Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error", empty otherwise.

status.description: Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way.

distinctId.description: DistinctID is the person/visitor the event is attributed to.

event.description: Event is the event name, e.g. page_viewed or signup_completed.

id.description:
ID is the row's stable event id — the client's own idempotency id when it sent
one, else the server-minted one.

path.description: Path is the URL's path component, the key the topPages lens groups by.

product.description: Product is the surface that emitted the event. Omitted when absent.

properties.description:
Properties is the row's attributes map as a JSON object (string values — the
plane stores Map(String,String), so a nested value the caller sent is a
JSON-encoded string). Omitted when the row carries none.

sessionId.description: SessionID groups the events of one visit. Omitted when the client sent none.

timestamp.description: Timestamp is when the event happened, RFC3339 UTC.

type.description:
Type is the row's kind — the plane's discriminator: page, track, identify or
group. (Errors are not here at all: they land on event.error and are read at
/v1/event/errors.)

url.description: URL is the full page address the event fired on. Omitted when absent.

active.description: Active is how long the person was active in it, in milliseconds.

blocks.description: Blocks is how many stored blocks hold it.

bytes.description: Bytes is the recording's size as the recorder sent it.

clicks.description: Clicks is how many clicks it caught.

end.description: End is its last frame, RFC3339 UTC.

keypresses.description: Keypresses is how many key presses it caught.

project.description: Project is the replay pipeline's project the recording is filed under.

start.description: Start is the recording's first frame, RFC3339 UTC.

url.description: URL is the first page recorded, with credential-shaped query values redacted.

end.description: End is its last frame, RFC3339 UTC.

error.description:
Error says why the block gave none — unreadable, sealed, or outside the
replay bucket. Omitted when it was read.

frames.description: Frames is how many frames the block gave.

start.description: Start is the block's first frame, RFC3339 UTC.

event.description: Event is the rrweb eventWithTime, verbatim: hand it to an rrweb player.

window.description: Window is the browser tab the event was recorded in.

data.description: Data is the visits, the most recent first. Null when the read failed.

degraded.description:
Degraded names a source that did not answer — "iam", or "replay" when the
recordings could not be read and every recording reads null for that reason.

msg.description: Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error", empty otherwise.

person.description: Person is who the visits are about. Null when the read failed.

status.description: Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way.

code.description: A stable token a client can branch on, when the refusal names one.

detail.description: What was refused, for a person to read.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
